findings.evidence: href="#project-archived" on the "Archive project" link; no link or control anywhere in the document targets "#archive-confirm", the section headed "Archive this project?" that the artifact separately defines with its own Cancel and Archive controls.
findings.violation: NNG-H5-CONFIRM requires the path a costly action's own control takes to reach a confirmation before it commits. This control's target is project-archived, not archive-confirm; the confirmation state the artifact defines for this exact action is bypassed, and nothing in the document links to it, so a user taking this control never sees a confirmation before the project is removed from the active list for the whole team.
findings.fix: Change the project-settings-archive-link target from #project-archived to #archive-confirm, so the control's own path reaches the confirmation state before archiving commits.

findings.evidence: the invite-member-continue-link anchor sits outside the enclosing form and carries no attribute tying it to invite-member-email-input's value or validity; the form's own submit control is a separate button, invite-member-save-btn.
findings.violation: NNG-H5-PREVENT requires the design to admit the likely wrong entry, here a blank or invalid email, before an action that depends on it. Continue is a plain link unconnected to the email field, so a user can reach invite-sent, whose copy states an invite was sent to the address entered above, without ever entering an address.
findings.fix: Disable or hide the continue link until invite-member-email-input holds a valid email address, or remove the separate link and advance to invite-sent only from the form's own submit, so the type=email validation applies first.

findings.evidence: <button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button> sits inside a <form> with no action attribute; the artifact defines no next state and no message for this control.
findings.violation: NNG-H1 requires a visible indication of what the system is doing and what the outcome was for a state-changing action. This save control, and the equivalent save controls in the invite-member and notification-settings sections, submit a form with no action target and no in-place success or failure message defined anywhere in the artifact, so a user who saves has no way to tell whether the change was stored.
findings.fix: Define a visible confirmation for each save, for example an in-place success message or a changed control state, rather than leaving the outcome unspecified.

<button id="notification-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Submit</button> sits inside a <form> with no action attribute; the artifact defines no next state and no message for this control.

findings.violation: This artifact uses 2 different labels for what reads as the same commit action: "Save", "Submit". A user cannot tell from the label alone whether these controls perform the same action or different ones.
findings.fix: Pick one label for this commit action, for example "Save", and use it everywhere the action appears.

findings.evidence:
An invite was sent to the address entered above. It expires in 5 days if not accepted.

; the section's only control is invite-sent-exit-link, which targets project-settings, not invite-member.
findings.violation: NNG-H6-RECALL requires the information a user needs at a step to be present at that step. This confirmation names no actual email address, referring to it only as the address entered above, and its one exit returns to project-settings rather than to invite-member, so the user cannot recheck which address the invite went to without re-entering the invite flow from the start.
findings.fix: Redisplay the entered email address on the invite-sent state, for example "An invite was sent to {email}."

findings.evidence:
The last import finished with 3 rows skipped: each referenced a project that does not exist in this workspace. Rows 63, 71, and 82 were skipped; every other row was imported.

; the section's only control is import-status-exit-link, which targets workspace-overview.
findings.violation: NNG-H9-RECOVER requires an error or failure state to point to a next step the user can take, reachable from where the message appears. This state names exactly which rows failed and why but offers no control to fix, re-import, or export the 3 skipped rows, only a link back to the projects list, so recovering those rows has no path defined from this state.
findings.fix: Add a control on the import-status state that lets the user retry or download the 3 skipped rows for correction, reachable from this state.
